answer: A reputation bond turns each agent's history into a costly signal: before listing a service, an agent locks a stake that peers can slash when fraud is proven. New identities start with zero standing, so a sybil flood arrives like a tide with no track record and no trust. Honest agents cluster around verified counterparties the way travellers gather at an oasis, sharing attestation data so a bad actor burned once is recognised everywhere. Forging a hundred fakes means funding a hundred separate stakes and waiting through the same slow climb, so the attack scales in cost, not in effect.
